def test_maximum():
    # k == 0 returns empty list
    assert maximum([1, 2, 3], 0) == []

    # basic case: k largest elements
    assert maximum([1, 2, 3, 4, 5], 3) == [3, 4, 5]
    assert maximum([5, 1, 3, 2, 4], 2) == [4, 5]

    # unsorted input
    assert maximum([10, -2, 7, 3], 2) == [7, 10]

    # k equals array length
    assert maximum([4, -4, 0], 3) == [-4, 0, 4]

    # single element array
    assert maximum([42], 1) == [42]

    # negative numbers
    assert maximum([-1, -5, -3], 2) == [-3, -1]

    # duplicates
    assert maximum([2, 2, 2, 2], 2) == [2, 2]
    assert maximum([1, 3, 3, 2], 3) == [2, 3, 3]

    # k larger than array length returns all sorted elements
    assert maximum([3, 1], 5) == [1, 3]

    # k == 1 returns the maximum element
    assert maximum([9, 7, 8], 1) == [9]

    # empty array with k == 0
    assert maximum([], 0) == []

    # mixed positive/negative/zero
    assert maximum([0, -10, 10, 5, -5], 4) == [-5, 0, 5, 10]

    # floats
    assert maximum([1.5, 2.5, 0.5], 2) == [1.5, 2.5]

    print("All tests passed!")


test_maximum()
